provider.name: FishBase
provider.organization_type: global finfish taxonomy, species accounts, distribution, ecology, life history, morphology, fisheries, aquaculture, conservation, occurrence, media, and bibliographic information system
provider.description: FishBase is a global information system for fishes. It integrates taxonomy, nomenclature, common names, distribution, ecology, life-history traits, population dynamics, reproduction, morphology, fisheries, aquaculture, conservation, introductions, museum records, photographs, references, maps, and calculated biological indicators.
institutional_context: WorldFish and historical FishBase development partners
Taxonomic experts, museums, fisheries agencies, and research institutions
SeaLifeBase and related biodiversity information infrastructure

purpose.summary: This file is a crawl-ready source catalog for collecting FishBase documentation, taxonomic and nomenclatural guidance, species-account field definitions, ecology and life-history methods, distribution, occurrences, fisheries, media, APIs, downloads, data dictionaries, licensing, citation instructions, and institutional context.
purpose.authoritative_notice: FishBase, its editors, cited source publications, and contributing institutions remain authoritative for species records, taxonomy, calculated fields, references, data versions, rights, and contact information.

notes: Verify whether a currently supported official FishBase API exists and whether fishbase.ropensci.org remains operational.
Treat rfishbase as a client and access layer, not automatically as the authoritative FishBase service.
Do not infer undocumented endpoints from browser traffic, old examples, or repository code.
Capture service ownership, backend database version, endpoint names, fields, paging, filters, limits, and legal conditions.
Capture exact FishBase legal wording before normalizing rights metadata.
Separate database facts, calculated biological values, source quotations, museum records, photos, drawings, maps, downloads, APIs, and software.
Preserve source reference, contributor, photographer, rights holder, license URI, database version, access date, and record identifier.
Do not assume FishBase availability grants rights to third-party photographs, maps, publications, or museum records.
Seed URLs are best-effort and were not live-verified in this session.
The acquisition program should update retrieval, content, review, and verification fields in place.
FishBase paths, mirror domains, manual pages, download files, API services, and rfishbase backends may move, redirect, or be retired; preserve redirect and failure metadata.
Do not recursively crawl every species page, synonym, country list, occurrence, museum record, photo, reference, or API result when the task is documentation acquisition.
Do not store passwords, API keys, cookies, OAuth tokens, account credentials, or session credentials in this JSON file.
Taxonomic facts, calculated traits, ecological records, museum records, photos, maps, references, downloads, APIs, and software may carry different rights.

Always preserve FishBase species code, accepted scientific name, synonym relationships, source references, database version, calculation method, confidence or caveat, media license, citation, and provenance.
